mentions.name: AgentOS
mentions.description: A deterministic, event-sourced runtime for agent worlds (agent substrates/sandboxes) that is fully replayable from its log. Heavy logic runs in sandboxed WASM modules, and every real-world side effect (HTTP, LLM calls, code compilations, etc.) is explicitly capability-gated and recorded as signed receipts, keeping upgrades and automations auditable, reversible, and composable. A small typed control-plane intermediate representation (AIR) treats the system's own schemas, modules, plans, and policies as data, enabling reliable, governed self-modification via a propose > shadow-run > approve > apply loop.
mentions.source_excerpt: I’m building AgentOS [1], trying to experiment where agent substrates/sandboxes will head next. It's a deterministic, event-sourced runtime where an “agent world” is replayable from its log, heavy logic runs in sandboxed WASM modules, and every real-world side effect (HTTP, LLM calls, code compilations, etc.) is explicitly capability-gated and recorded as signed receipts.

mentions.name: AgentOS
mentions.description: AgentOS is a low-level, lisp-machine inspired runtime for AI agents. Agents can safely propose, simulate, and apply changes to their own code, policies, and workflows under governance, with full audit trails: every external action produces a signed receipt and every state change is replayable from an event log.
mentions.source_excerpt: AgentOS is a lisp-machine inspired runtime where agents can safely propose, simulate, and apply changes to their own code, policies, and workflows, all under governance, with full audit trails. Every external action produces a signed receipt. Every state change is replayable from an event log.
